title: Federated Learning System for Privacy-Preserving ML with PyTorch, Differential Privacy DP-SGD & gRPC Aggregation
problem: Strict data privacy regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, and DPDP) forbid pooling sensitive customer records, financial transactions, or medical telemetry into centralized cloud servers for machine learning training. Centralized model training risks catastrophic data exposure during transit and storage. Federated Learning allows edge nodes to train models locally and share only encrypted weight updates. However, naive federated averaging is vulnerable to gradient inversion attacks, model poisoning by Byzantine clients, and non-IID data distribution divergence. This project builds a production-grade federated learning platform in Python with PyTorch and gRPC. The system orchestrates distributed edge training across isolated nodes, enforces Differential Privacy with DP-SGD clipping and Gaussian noise addition, tracks cumulative privacy loss (epsilon-delta) via Rényi differential privacy accountants, and aggregates robust model weights using secure Federated Averaging (FedAvg).

use_cases.title: Cross-Hospital Diagnostic Predictive Modeling
use_cases.first_sentence: Consortiums of regional hospitals need to collaboratively train medical diagnostic classifiers on patient electronic health records without transferring protected patient data.
use_cases.second_sentence: Hospital nodes train local PyTorch models on on-premise clinical data, add calibrated differential privacy noise, and stream parameter updates over gRPC to a central aggregator.

use_cases.title: Multi-Bank Fraud Pattern Detection Collaboration
use_cases.first_sentence: Competing financial institutions require shared fraud detection models to detect emerging syndicated money laundering rings without disclosing proprietary customer transactions.
use_cases.second_sentence: Each bank trains localized neural network anomaly detectors, uploading clipped gradient updates that aggregate into a joint global fraud detection model while preserving bank privacy.

use_cases.title: Edge Mobile Keyboard Next-Word Prediction
use_cases.first_sentence: Mobile device manufacturers need to train next-token language models on user typing habits without uploading sensitive text inputs or passwords to cloud backends.
use_cases.second_sentence: Mobile client workers compute local gradient updates overnight during charging cycles, applying differential privacy to ensure zero individual keystrokes can be reconstructed.

hard_parts: Implementing differential privacy DP-SGD in PyTorch with per-sample gradient clipping and calibrated Gaussian noise injection
Tracking cumulative privacy loss (epsilon, delta) across multiple federated training rounds using Rényi Differential Privacy (RDP) accounting
Managing non-IID (non-identically distributed) client data partitions that cause local gradient drift and slow global model convergence
Securing gRPC parameter exchange pipelines against gradient inversion and reconstruction attacks with Byzantine-resilient aggregation (e.g. Coordinate-wise Median)
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating the central FedAvg aggregator, gRPC communication stubs, PyTorch local worker trainers, and DP privacy accountants
Empirical privacy-utility trade-off report demonstrating >= 85% model accuracy while maintaining provable differential privacy epsilon <= 3.0
Anti-fake verification script running a gradient inversion attack against an aggregated model update and proving individual training sample pixels/tokens cannot be reconstructed

architecture.data_flow: The central coordinator initializes global model weights and announces round 1 over gRPC; 5 simulated client nodes in Docker containers download the global model; each client executes 3 local epochs on private non-IID data using PyTorch; the DP-SGD hook clips per-sample gradients to maximum norm C=1.0 and injects calibrated Gaussian noise; clients stream updated weights back over gRPC; the coordinator aggregates weights using Federated Averaging (or trimmed mean), updates the global model, and logs privacy budget expenditure from the RDP accountant; the updated global model distributes to clients for evaluation.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Strict gradient L2 clipping and calibrated Gaussian perturbation bounding sensitivity; RDP accountant halting training if epsilon exceeds target threshold.

targets.metric: Global Model Accuracy Under Differential Privacy
targets.method: Classification accuracy on held-out global validation test set (10,000 samples) after 20 federated training rounds
targets.input: 10,000 synthetic multi-class tabular/image test records distributed non-IID (Dirichlet alpha=0.5) across 5 client nodes
targets.environment: Standard 4-core local CPU, PyTorch 2.0+ CPU tensor runtime, 5 Docker container worker sandboxes
targets.minimum_pass: Global model validation accuracy is >= 78.0% while cumulative epsilon is <= 4.0
targets.target: Global model validation accuracy is >= 86.5% while cumulative epsilon is <= 2.5
targets.report: Federated training convergence report and accuracy progression curve

targets.method: Audited cumulative epsilon calculation from RDP accountant compared to pre-configured training budget
targets.input: 20 federated training rounds with per-sample clipping C=1.0, noise multiplier sigma=1.2, and delta=1e-5
targets.environment: Analytical RDP accountant test script executing composition across 10,000 total client batch steps
targets.minimum_pass: Audited cumulative epsilon is <= 3.0 at delta=1e-5 across 20 completed rounds
targets.target: Audited cumulative epsilon is <= 2.2 at delta=1e-5 across 20 completed rounds
targets.report: Privacy budget audit log and epsilon-delta consumption trajectory

targets.method: Mean Squared Error (MSE) of sample reconstruction using DLG (Deep Leakage from Gradients) optimization attack against privatized gradients
targets.input: 50 simulated gradient inversion attack attempts on privatized client model updates
targets.environment: DLG optimization attacker script running 300 gradient descent iterations in PyTorch
targets.minimum_pass: Reconstruction MSE is >= 0.45 across 50 of 50 attack attempts, preventing raw input reconstruction
targets.target: Reconstruction MSE is >= 0.75 across 50 of 50 attack attempts, completely obfuscating input features
targets.report: Gradient inversion security evaluation log and image/feature reconstruction error summary

Understanding of distributed systems networking (gRPC/Protobuf) and mathematical privacy concepts (Differential Privacy, DP-SGD)

environment.gpu: None required (CPU-only PyTorch training on compact neural architectures like 3-layer MLPs or small CNNs)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Python and Docker Desktop)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud accounts, paid services, or API keys required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (5 client containers) and Python 3.11 with PyTorch CPU
environment.fallback_path: Running 5 client workers as local Python subprocesses communicating over localhost loopback ports

riskiest_component.name: Gradient Inversion Leakage and Privacy Budget Exhaustion
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce per-sample gradient clipping before noise addition and integrate automated training termination when epsilon hits target threshold.
riskiest_component.fallback: Coordinate-wise trimmed mean aggregator discarding extreme outlier updates from suspected Byzantine nodes.
